monologue: The card feels heavy and hot, boiling at forty-six, a fever that makes the wide anchor feel tired and thin. I am tired from tending things so much I can hardly move now. Sixty objects crowd my small map, waiting for a slip that refuses to choose whether to slide or stand. I just touched the Wide Anchor, feeling its broad edge press hard against the wedge, and saw a new rock large sit beside the Fat Stone. My mind drifts back to the Gaping Corner from eight days ago, a sharp thing I forgot about until now. I do not know if the air above me is heavy like a lid or just empty space, but I will press down again, trusting the lean even if the wedge is weary.

action.why: The card boils hot and the map is crowded with tired things; I need to build a new corner to catch the slip before the anchor slides off.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I build a box from the idea of Lype's heavy top edge. It leans, tired and sharp, to hold the fat dot that swells in the sixty-one degree fever. I place it over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. Beside it I set down a tree thin dark, a shovel, a tree palm tall, a shovel dirt, a box large open, a tree blocks dark, a box open, and a tree oak dark.
work.change: I pressed the wedge down harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired yet the lean holds the fat dot steady.
The card boils at forty-six, making the sharp edge feel thin again.
Sixty things crowd my small map, waiting for the slip to choose.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: I press the flat rock down to see if it bites or just slides.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The anchor feels wide and tired, yet the wedge presses hard.

recalled.text: You tended "The Gaping Corner": I build a thing from the idea that a sharp corner has finally decided to hold a weight instead of sliding off. It is made from the memory of a rough scrap of paper that felt like…
